objective: A member can permanently delete their account and everything tied to it, after a clear warning and their password, leaving other people's posts intact and nothing identifying behind.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: USERS-006 has merged to main, and the Director PR that adds cognito-idp:AdminDeleteUser to infra/iam/fanwire-role-boundary-policy.json has merged and been applied to AWS by the human, with the policy version named in the PR body. Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test.

DELETE /users/me/data answers 204 for the caller's own account only, on the identity path so that a retry after a partial failure still works. It reads no user id from the request, and requires auth_time within 5 minutes, else 403 recent_auth_required. test_route_auth.py's allowlist gains exactly this route.

After a 204 the database holds no row for the user in users, follows (either side), notification_preferences, notifications (as recipient or actor, or with a reference_id naming one of their removed posts or themselves), post_likes, reports, media or event_mentions of a removed post. A test walks every foreign key to users in Base.metadata, so a future table cannot be forgotten.
Likes and reports by others on the user's posts are removed with those posts.

A post of theirs that no one else's surviving post depends on is deleted. A post that another user's reply or repost depends on, directly or through a chain of their own posts, becomes a tombstone: author_id null, text null, every linked_* null, deleted_at set, and no media.

posts.author_id becomes nullable with a CHECK that a null author requires deleted_at. No API response ever shows a tombstone as a post: other users' threads show the existing root_deleted card and the existing Post deleted box. A test covers thread, feed, search, a quote repost and a plain repost by another user.

Every S3 object the user's media rows name, in the quarantine and public buckets, is deleted. The API function gains s3:DeleteObject on those buckets' object ARNs and cognito-idp:AdminDeleteUser on this pool's ARN only, and iam-policy.test.ts and permissions-boundary.test.ts pass.

Order: S3 objects, then the database in one transaction, then AdminDeleteUser. A failure at any step answers 5xx with nothing later done, and repeating the request finishes the job. Tests force a failure at each step and then repeat. A caller with no User row and a valid token goes straight to AdminDeleteUser. An identity Cognito no longer has counts as done.
Each module removes its own rows through its own service function, and one orchestrator calls them in a single transaction. No module reaches into another's tables, per the Connection rule.
Logs for this flow carry only the local user id and counts, never the email, username or sub.
The notifications consumer drops an event whose actor, recipient or post no longer exists, with a log line, instead of raising MissingReferenceError into the DLQ. A test covers each case.

/settings adds, last, a destructive button 'Delete my data'. It opens a dialog titled 'Delete all your data?' that says plainly this cannot be undone and that recovery is not possible; lists account, profile, posts, replies, likes, reposts, follows, notifications and images; says replies other people wrote stay; and says backup copies expire within 7 days.

The dialog has a labelled password input, and its 'Delete my data' button is disabled until the input is not empty. Confirm re-authenticates through USERS-006's reauthenticate, then calls the route. A wrong password stays in the dialog and makes no call. A failed call shows an alert that nothing is lost by trying again.
On success the app signs out and clears its cache, then lands on / and announces 'Your account and data have been deleted.' Signing in again with those credentials fails.

Browser row on localhost with a throwaway dev-pool account, with evidence or NOT DONE: a populated account including a post someone else replied to and an uploaded image is deleted, the database rows and S3 objects are checked afterwards, and the other user's reply still shows under the Post deleted card.
frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/USERS-008.ts declares, in the test commit, every output the unit changes. Entry growth is at most 2 KiB raw and 1 KiB gzip, and no output reaches 500,000 raw bytes.
No new dependency. boto3 is already present.

wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x01-users.md, 0x03-posts.md, 0x04-media.md, 0x05-notifications.md and 0x08-frontend.md record the rule, including that soft delete stays the default and this is the one hard delete.
